rules.description: CUTSCENE_SCRIPT_V1 has one first-class moves[] vocabulary with exactly 53 legal moves. Each move has an exact CURRENT id and references consecutive beatIds in film order. The number of beatIds must equal that move's published phase count. Every referenced beat must visibly satisfy the published cinematicSignature and that phase's machine-readable phaseRequirements, and the full move must satisfy any published wholeMoveConstraints. Within phaseRequirements, every allOf entry must pass and anyOf means at least one listed V1 predicate must be authored. wholeMoveConstraints are cross-phase identity, co-presence, intent and shared-direction requirements from the same canonical validator, not optional prose. Use existing V1 motionIntent, camera, visible composition, action and path fields to satisfy those predicates and make the signature observable; a move id is not a decorative label. moves[] is the only move field. Do not author backend implementation fields or raw runtime IDs. Current repertoire: 1. CROSSING_FLYBY [enter -> pass_camera -> exit] signature={Traveler must visibly traverse the frame in one direction: enter may be an explicit enter action or an authored path from outside to inside frame; pass uses flyby/pass_camera motion; exit may be an explicit exit action or an authored path from inside to outside frame.}; 2. HERO_SWEEP [flyby -> foreground_arc -> bank_away -> exit] signature={Hero performs a readable flyby or foreground arc, then banks away and exits with a clear change of direction.}; 3. ATTACK_RUN [approach -> fire_during_pass -> pass_camera -> bank_away] signature={Attacker approaches target, fires during the pass, crosses camera/target space, then banks away.}; 4. BOOM_AND_BREAK [attack -> impact -> formation_break -> clear_blast] signature={Attack produces a visible impact/explosion and the formation visibly breaks away from the blast.}; 5. DOUBLE_INTERCEPT [separate_defenders -> converge -> hold_intercept_lane] signature={Two distinct interceptors converge on one target from separate lanes and finish in a readable intercept geometry.}; 6. FLANK_LEFT [peel_left -> arc_intercept -> hold_target_readability] signature={Left flanker peels to a left-side lane, curves toward the target, then holds a readable flanking relation.}; 7. FLANK_RIGHT [peel_right -> arc_intercept -> hold_target_readability] signature={Right flanker peels to a right-side lane, curves toward the target, then holds a readable flanking relation.}; 8. PURSUIT_LANES [establish_depth_lanes -> parallel_pursuit -> closing_gap] signature={Pursuer and pursued occupy distinct lanes/depths while moving in the same travel direction and the gap visibly closes.}; 9. CHASE_THROUGH_FRAME [target_crosses -> chasers_enter -> same_direction_exit] signature={Pursued crosses first; pursuer enters after it and both leave in the same screen direction.}; 10. ESCORT_COLUMN [principal_leads -> escorts_hold_spacing -> shared_travel] signature={Principal leads while escorts maintain distinct spacing and share one travel direction.}; 11. ESCORT_PEEL_OFF [escort -> peel_off -> bank_away -> exit] signature={Escort formation is established, at least one escort peels away, banks, and exits while protected subject remains readable.}; 12. FORMATION_SPREAD [stable_formation -> open_spacing -> hold] signature={At least three formation members begin grouped, increase separation, then hold the wider formation.}; 13. FORMATION_CONVERGE [separate_entries -> converge_to_slots -> hold] signature={At least three members enter from separated positions, converge toward formation slots, then hold.}; 14. BANK_AND_EXIT [bank_away -> accelerate -> exit] signature={Traveler performs a bank-away curve, accelerates, and leaves the frame.}; 15. FORMATION_RETREAT [formation_break -> retreat_lanes -> exit] signature={Formation breaks under threat, members retreat in readable lanes, then exit in a shared retreat direction.}; 16. DAMAGED_WITHDRAWAL [impact_or_react -> brief_hold -> crippled_drift -> escape] signature={Damage/impact reaction is followed by a brief readable hold, impaired drift, then escape.}; 17. TAKEOFF_ESCORT [takeoff -> escort_join -> shared_travel] signature={Takeoff actor visibly launches, escort joins, and both continue in shared travel.}; 18. LAUNCH_WAVE [staggered_takeoffs -> clear_launch_area] signature={Multiple launched actors take off with staggered timing and clear the launch area.}; 19. LANDING_APPROACH [approach -> landing -> settle_hold] signature={Lander approaches, performs landing motion, then settles into a hold.}; 20. LAND_THEN_GUARD_ORBIT [landing -> center_stops -> guards_orbit] signature={Center lands and becomes stationary while at least two guards orbit that fixed center.}; 21. STATIC_CENTER_ORBIT_REVEAL [static_center -> guard_orbit -> pull_reveal -> hold] signature={Center remains static while orbiters circle it; camera pulls to reveal the full scale/context.}; 22. ORBIT_THEN_BREAK [orbit -> break -> bank_away] signature={Orbit is visibly established before orbiters break formation and bank away.}; 23. RESCUE_PASS [rescue_approach -> visible_meet -> escort_escape] signature={Rescuer approaches rescued subject, they visibly meet/share frame, then the same rescuer and rescued subject both escape with authored displacement in a shared direction.}; 24. CONVOY_ESCAPE [convoy_travel -> threat_pressure -> escape_same_direction] signature={Leader/protected/escort travel as convoy under threat and escape in a shared direction.}; 25. THREAT_REVEAL_PASS [foreground_pass -> threat_revealed -> pull_scale_context] signature={Foreground passer crosses/occludes, revealing a threat behind it; camera pull establishes threat scale/context.}; 26. VICTORY_FLYBY [formation_flyby -> celebratory_break -> exit] signature={Multiple ships perform a readable formation flyby, celebratory break, then exit.}; 27. QUIET_DRIFT_OUT [slow_drift -> quiet_exit] signature={Retreating actor uses slow drift with restrained camera and exits without impact-shake/combat punctuation.}; 28. SCREEN_CROSS_REVEAL [foreground_occlusion -> cross_frame -> target_revealed] signature={Foreground occluder crosses the frame and genuinely hides then reveals the hidden subject.}; 29. CROSS_TRAFFIC [lane_a_cross -> lane_b_cross_other_depth -> clear_readable_flow] signature={Two traffic groups cross in distinct lanes/depths and directions while remaining visually separable.}; 30. HOLD_THEN_BURST [hold -> burst_acceleration -> travel_payoff] signature={Traveler begins in a genuine hold, then switches to burst-speed displacement with a clear travel payoff.}; 31. ARRIVE_SETTLE_HOLD [arrive -> decelerate_settle -> hold] signature={Same arriving actor approaches, slows, and the authored settle path ends at the position used by the following held beat; the final composition remains static there.}; 32. TARGET_LOCK [attacker_establish -> target_cut -> attacker_push_in -> fire] signature={Attacker establish -> target cut -> tighter attacker push/track -> explicit fire.}; 33. LOOK_REVEAL_REACTION [looking_face -> seen_subject -> reaction_push_in] signature={Looker is shown looking, observed subject is revealed, then reaction returns to the looker with tighter emphasis.}; 34. THREAT_APPROACH [subject -> distant_threat -> subject_return -> closer_threat -> reaction_closeup] signature={Alternating subject/threat shots show the threat materially closer on its second appearance, ending on subject reaction.}; 35. FALSE_DIRECTION_ATTACK [attacker_exits -> target_hold -> offscreen_attack_from_implied_direction -> impact] signature={Attacker exits, target holds, attack returns from the implied offscreen direction, then impact lands.}; 36. rules.description: For NEW movies, author a brisk cinematic tempo by default, not prolonged wide shots or motionless holds. Most MOVES/action beats should last roughly 1.4 to 2.8 seconds, fast impacts 0.5 to 1.2 seconds, and establishing/reveal shots 2.0 to 3.5 seconds only when comprehension needs them. A 90-second action film usually needs about 25 to 35 meaningful visible developments, not a handful of stretched shots. Use actions[].speed=fast for ship travel and burst for chase/flyby/escape when appropriate, with enough screen displacement for motion to read. Use short readable captions for roughly 0.9 to 1.8 seconds, concurrent compatible visual and sound actions, and motivated cuts instead of empty pauses. Let spoken dialogue finish naturally; use deliberate emotional holds and intentionally slow moments where the story requires them. To honor a requested total runtime, add meaningful events instead of stretching movements. Preserve explicitly chosen timing when repairing an existing movie. Author no new JSON fields.
